findings.title: Collections Were Not Always Deposited Timely Nor Adequately Secured Prior to Deposit
findings.description: Collections totaling approximately $10 million were not always deposited timely and SCPS had not established adequate controls over collections received at the Central Office. A test of 10 deposits disclosed that collections totaling $452,000 related to 6 deposits were deposited from 3 to 13 working days after receipt.

dollar_amounts.context: collections received at the Central Office
funds received by check from Somerset County
test of 10 deposits
collections deposited untimely

findings.recommendation: SCPS should deposit all funds in a timely manner, properly safeguard cash receipts prior to deposit, and investigate with the Somerset County government the possibility of receiving funds by electronic transfer rather than check.

findings.title: SCPS Lacked Written Policies and Procedures for Controlling Student Activity Funds
findings.description: SCPS did not have written policies and procedures for controlling student activity funds. Control deficiencies were noted at two high schools which collected $242,324 or 42 percent of the total student activity funds.

dollar_amounts.context: student activity fund collections at two high schools

findings.recommendation: SCPS should develop policies and procedures governing controls and accountability over student activity funds, and ensure that the developed procedures are followed.

findings.title: Users’ Capabilities on the Automated Procurement and Accounts Payable System Were Not Adequately Restricted
findings.description: SCPS did not adequately restrict users’ capabilities to prevent unauthorized purchasing and disbursement transactions. Five employees could initiate and approve purchase orders without independent approvals.
findings.recommendation: SCPS should strengthen its controls over the automated procurement and accounts payable system by restricting users’ capabilities to eliminate incompatible duties and establishing independent electronic approval requirements.

findings.title: SCPS’ Procurement Policies Generally Did Not Require Board Approval for Certain Purchases and Did Not Address Contractual Services
findings.description: SCPS policies did not require Board approval for the majority of high-value purchases. Disbursements to 10 vendors totaling approximately $1.2 million were not approved by the Board.

dollar_amounts.context: disbursements to 10 vendors not approved by the Board

findings.recommendation: SCPS should amend its existing policies for procurement to address all categories of purchases and establish a formal dollar threshold requiring Board approval.

findings.title: Contracts Were Frequently Not Awarded Through Competitive Procurements and Payment Processing Was Not Always Adequate
findings.description: A test of payments to 12 vendors disclosed that 10 contractors with fiscal year 2013 payments totaling $1.2 million were selected without competitive procurements. Overpayments of $68,000 occurred due to miscalculated fuel adjustments.

dollar_amounts.context: payments to 12 vendors
payments to 10 contractors without competitive procurements
payments to three vendors with insufficient review
overpayments due to miscalculated fuel adjustments

findings.recommendation: SCPS should award contracts through competitive procurement methods or document why they cannot be used, prepare written contracts, use eMaryland Marketplace, and ensure vendor payments are proper.

findings.title: Independent Reviews of Payroll and Personnel Transactions Processed Were Lacking
findings.description: SCPS lacked an independent review to ensure that processed employee personnel and payroll transactions were correct. Two overpayments totaling $2,450 and five underpaid terminated employees totaling $13,395 were noted.

dollar_amounts.context: overpayment to one terminated employee
underpayments to five terminated employees

findings.recommendation: SCPS should perform a documented independent review of personnel and payroll transactions, resolve the noted payment errors, limit assignments of critical system functions, and eliminate incompatible functions.

findings.title: Documentation Was Lacking That the Board Possessed All Pertinent Information Prior to Approving an Employee Termination Settlement Agreement
findings.description: There was no documentation that the Board possessed pertinent information prior to approving a settlement agreement totaling $168,000 for a former school official.

dollar_amounts.context: employee contract settlement agreement

findings.recommendation: SCPS should ensure that all pertinent information is provided to the Board regarding contract interpretations and related fiscal impact for any future contract settlements.

findings.title: Equipment Policies Were Not Comprehensive and Disposals Were Not Approved
findings.description: SCPS did not obtain approval from supervisory personnel to dispose of equipment. Review disclosed 100 items marked as disposed with a cost totaling approximately $91,000.

dollar_amounts.context: cost of items marked as disposed without approval

findings.recommendation: SCPS should update its existing procedures to include requirements for segregating duties and performing physical inventories, and obtain required approval of all disposals of equipment.

findings.title: SCPS’ Network Was Not Adequately Secured and Certain User Capabilities Were Not Properly Restricted
findings.description: The SCPS network was not properly secured from improper access by students. Local administrator privileges were not properly restricted on workstations.
findings.recommendation: SCPS should implement controls to limit network level student access, limit local administrative rights on user workstations, and disable settings allowing users to override security controls.

findings.title: Monitoring, Account, and Password Controls Over SCPS’ Academic System Were Not Sufficient
findings.description: The database supporting the academic information application was not configured to log security activity. Account and password controls were not in accordance with best practice guidelines.
findings.recommendation: SCPS should enable logging of all critical database security activities and implement recommended account and password settings over the academic information application.

findings.title: Certain Construction Related Goods and Services Were Procured Without Obtaining Competitive Bids
findings.description: SCPS executed a $98,000 change order that materially altered the scope of a project rather than seeking bids. SCPS did not receive competitive bids for a $223,000 contract.

dollar_amounts.context: construction related goods and services procured without competitive bids
change order amount
original contract amount
contract without competitive bids
travel expenses included in payments to contractor

findings.recommendation: SCPS should not use change orders for tasks that materially alter the scope of the original project and obtain goods and services through a documented competitive procurement process.

findings.title: Certain Payments to Transportation Contractors Were Not Based on Market Conditions or Actual Costs
findings.description: SCPS could not justify the 9.93 percent ROI rate used for bus contractors. Overpayments of $670,000 were estimated over the life of seven buses. SCPS paid $116,000 more than necessary due to federal fuel excise taxes.

dollar_amounts.context: potential cost savings over the life of seven buses
total fuel payments higher than necessary due to excise taxes

findings.recommendation: SCPS should establish payment amounts to transportation contractors in a manner that ensures all costs are reasonable and necessary.

findings.title: SCPS Did Not Ensure the Accuracy of Data Used to Compute Certain Payments to Bus Contractors
findings.description: SCPS did not ensure the accuracy of time and mileage payments to bus contractors. Hourly payments and base mileage payments totaled approximately $1 million.

dollar_amounts.context: hourly payments and base mileage payments to contractors

findings.recommendation: SCPS should independently verify bus contractor’s manifests, document the verification process, and recover any overpayments.

findings.title: Invoices Were Not Adequately Verified Prior to Payment
findings.description: A test of 10 invoices totaling $168,324 disclosed no evidence of a documented review for propriety prior to payment. Three vendors had purchases of $175,000 without formal contracts.

dollar_amounts.context: test of invoices
food expenditures for vendors tested
purchases from three vendors without formal contracts
purchases from two vendors with contracts not approved by Board
total food expenditures for fiscal year 2013

findings.recommendation: SCPS should ensure that formal contracts are executed with vendors and approved by the Board, and invoice prices are compared to contract prices prior to payment.

findings.title: Financial Disclosure Statements Were Not Always Filed As Required
findings.description: SCPS did not ensure that a financial disclosure statement was filed by all employees required to do so. Three of 11 employees required for calendar year 2012 did not file.
findings.recommendation: SCPS should actively enforce its ethics policy and ensure that all required disclosure statements are filed and reviewed by the ethics panel.

findings.title: SCPS Did Not Ensure the Propriety of Payments for Certain Employee and Retiree Health Care Costs
findings.description: SCPS lacked procedures to ensure that amounts paid to the third-party administrator were proper. Stop-loss insurance paid by SCPS totaled approximately $271,000.

dollar_amounts.context: amounts paid for health care during fiscal year 2013
administrative fees included in health care payments
stop-loss insurance paid by SCPS

findings.recommendation: SCPS should establish procedures to verify the amounts paid for health insurance.

extraction.agency_response_summary: SCPS generally agreed with the recommendations (Finding 4 was disagreed with; Findings 9 and 10 were agreed with exceptions). The agency outlined specific implementation steps for each finding in their response appendix.
